hard_rules._min_market_cap_note: Hard floor: never BUY a company under $1B market cap. Enforced at proposal validation (when a cap is known), at scanner surfacing, and at weekly universe review (sub-$1B adds are dropped like unpriceable names).

swing_rules._engagement_note: ADDED 2026-08-03. Every other fix this month was PERMISSIVE - it removed obstacles. None created a reason to ACT, and the record says obstacles were never the binding constraint: of 30 logged rejections ZERO failed on risk_reward_ratio or target upside and only 2 on confidence, while 165 runs produced 11 proposals. The real gap was that inaction was free. A fired watchlist trigger's only consequence anywhere in the codebase was a shadow-book row graded weeks later, so ANET and GE reached their own stated levels across four separate runs on 07-23/24 at no cost; and the shadow book has been BINDING for weeks (56 closed, 23 regret_miss vs 33 good_skip, threshold 8) with nothing downstream of it. max_unbought_trigger_hits: after this many DISTINCT DAYS at its own stated level without a buy, a watchlist name is force-dropped and must be re-underwritten from scratch rather than inherited. commitment_after_flat_days: once the book has been effectively all cash this many consecutive days, a no-trade run owes a `waiting_for` {ticker, condition, by_date} - a DATED condition, because an undated one cannot be graded and becomes a renewable excuse. NEITHER forces a trade: a fabricated setup teaches the learning loops garbage and is strictly worse than silence. They force a DECISION and a COMMITMENT.

position_sizing._notional_cap_note: Notional ceilings only. Risk-based sizing below is the binding constraint: a tight-stop setup may size up to these ceilings for the same 1% risk; a wide-stop setup sizes well under them. Raised from 10%/$1000 when risk-based sizing landed (2026-07-16). Rebased 10x DOWN on 2026-07-21 when the book was restated from a $10,000 start to a $1,000 start: every percentage stays identical, only the notional ceilings moved ($2000 -> $200, conviction $3000 -> $300, min clamp $200 -> $20). See _fractional_stop_note below — the smaller book changes what the broker can protect.

risk_based_sizing._note: Van Tharp / Elder / Turtle framework (research 2026-07-16, user-approved). Every BUY risks at most risk_per_trade_pct of equity measured entry-to-stop; the validator CLAMPS oversized proposals down to the risk budget rather than rejecting. Portfolio heat = sum over open positions of entry-basis committed risk max(0,(avg_cost-stop)*qty)/equity; new BUYs are rejected past portfolio_heat_cap_pct (user chose 8%; literature 6-10%). Theme cap: committed initial risk sharing one demand_driver <= theme_initial_risk_cap_pct. Entry-basis heat means trailed stops above cost free the budget (pyramiding into winners stays possible). momentum_unwind_risk_scale halves the risk budget when momentum_health flags an unwind.

scale_in._note: Adds allowed only into winners (price above blended cost, never averaging down), max 2 adds, combined exposure stays inside the per-name cap. Partial exits via sell_fraction in (0,1].

conviction_tier._note: When earned, conviction raises the RISK budget to 1.5% (and the notional ceilings accordingly); base tier stays 1%.

position_sizing._fractional_stop_note: CONSEQUENCE OF THE $1,000 BOOK, measured 2026-07-21 against the live 187-name universe. Alpaca carries fractional quantities only with time_in_force=day, so a GTC stop needs a whole-share leg (execution/alpaca_broker.py, MIN_WHOLE_SHARES_FOR_LIMIT=4 and _resting stop arming). At a $1,429 position (the $10,000 book) 69.5% of the universe got a full exchange-held GTC stop attached at entry and only 2.1% fell under one share. At a $143 position (this book) those become 3.2% and 72.2%: most entries are now sub-one-share, so their protective stop is a DAY order that expires at the close and is re-armed by scripts/stop_watch.py on the Actions cron. Intraday protection is a real resting broker order and is essentially unchanged; what is lost is the overnight/weekend leg, where the exit now depends on the poller's next tick rather than the opening print. Accepted deliberately: the gap risk is real but denominated in single-digit dollars at this size. Do NOT read a low whole-share count as a reason to skip a setup.

trade_quality_requirements._variant_perception_note: Every BUY must state the market's misunderstanding explicitly: what consensus believes, what the agent believes differently, the specific mispriced mechanism, and the event/date when the market finds out. Enforced as a required BUY field; format documented in CLAUDE.md.
trade_quality_requirements._risk_map_scenarios_note: risk_map and scenarios were always in the CLAUDE.md schema but not validator-enforced, so proposals omitted scenarios and the published scenario_ev stayed empty. Now required on every BUY.
trade_quality_requirements._thesis_invalidators_note: Binding falsifiers (not vibes): object with invalidating_print, invalidating_structure, time_box — each a non-empty string. Enforced on every BUY so re-underwrites have kill criteria.
trade_quality_requirements._demand_driver_note: Primary demand-driver theme for theme concentration (e.g. hyperscaler_server_capex, ai_compute_gpu). Distinct from GICS sector. See tools/demand_drivers.py and context bundle demand_driver_map.
trade_quality_requirements._required_sell_fields_note: SELL_TO_CLOSE needs only these; the BUY-oriented required_proposal_fields list used to reject legitimate discretionary exits for missing stop_loss/target_price. Prefer also exit_reason when available (process, not hard-required).
trade_quality_requirements._claim_grounding_note: Added 2026-07-25, DEFAULT OFF pending evidence, same staged rollout as _tradeability_note below. WHAT IT DOES: validator._check_claim_grounding greps every entity a BUY's variant_perception/catalysts name against the FULL context bundle and rejects the ones that appear nowhere in it. Built from four real incidents the LLM risk desk caught by hand: DDOG 07-22 ('JMP Securities raised its target to $311' - the string 'JMP' appears ZERO times in that day's bundle), MELI 07-24 ('Loggi acquisition', a Citi fair-value cut, '14 new Brazil fulfillment centers'), IBKR 07-22 (an invented 'fourth consecutive beat' with an EMPTY guidance_ledger), UNP 07-24 (a 'binding MOU signed one day earlier' that inverts the actual sequence). WHY IT IS NOT ON YET: CLAUDE.md step 5 makes WebSearch MANDATORY before any BUY, so the brain is REQUIRED to bring in facts that legitimately are not in the bundle - blocking on 'absent from bundle' would reject true WebSearch findings alongside fabricated ones, and a false rejection costs a real trade on a book that has already gone days without one. Until proposals carry per-claim sources, the SAME computation is fed to the risk desk every run (validator.unsourced_claims -> runlib.brain_io), which can weigh the WebSearch context a regex cannot. TO ENABLE: watch the risk-desk prompt's UNSOURCED CLAIMS block for a week; if the entities it lists are consistently real fabrications rather than WebSearch-sourced truth, flip this to true. Precision was tuned against the 7 real BUY proposals in journal/proposals + journal/rejected: multi-word candidates are only taken from an explicit attribution pattern ('<Firm> raised/said/cut'), because the bare proper-noun pass produced prose fragments like 'MINIMUM CONTRACTED' and 'Case After Strong' that no bundle would ever contain verbatim.

calibration_probe._note: ADDED 2026-08-05. A BUY scored honestly in [0.50, 0.60) is no longer rejected outright: it trades as a CALIBRATION PROBE at risk_scale x the normal risk budget (0.5% of equity instead of 1%), stamped calibration_probe on the proposal AND persisted onto the position's plan at fill, with at most max_open_probes such positions on the book at once (validator._check_probe_limits). WHY: the hard 0.60 floor could never learn whether 0.50-0.60 setups win, because it never let one trade - HPE on 2026-08-05 died at 0.57 the same afternoon a validated DXCM entry died on a keyword false-positive, on a book that had made 3 trades in a month - and its only lasting lesson to the proposer was that honesty costs the trade while writing 0.62 sails through. The desk's confidence haircut (max -0.10) previously turned into a death sentence whenever it landed under 0.60; now it converts the trade to half-risk instead, so the desk can express skepticism without killing the setup. Probe fills grade into their own 0.50-0.60 bucket (tools/performance_breakdown._confidence_bucket), so once 5+ close the existing calibration machinery has REAL fill data: if the bucket proves losing (<40% WR) the losing-bucket gate starts rejecting it with evidence, and if it proves fine that argues the floor down. Every other gate - RR>=2, geometry, volatility stop, heat, theme caps, earnings window, risk desk - applies to a probe at full strength; below probe min_confidence remains a hard rejection.

earnings_window._note: ADDED 2026-08-03. Until now there was NO coded earnings rule anywhere - `days_to_earnings` appeared ZERO times in validator.py - so 'trade around the binary' was entirely the brain's judgment applied against a 45-day default horizon. In earnings season that excludes essentially the whole universe, and it did: across 2026-07-13..08-03 run after run passed on every candidate for a print somewhere inside the swing window (08-03 alone rejected MPC and AMGN for an 08-04 print, then NET and TEAM for 08-06, and traded nothing). The gate is now NARROW and the narrowness is the point: only a print within pre_print_blackout_days blocks a BUY, everything outside it is explicitly tradeable, and a name that has ALREADY reported within post_print_drift_days is a PREFERRED lane (the binary is resolved and the geometry is clean). allow_trade_through_with_case lets the brain trade the print deliberately when the binary IS the thesis, by supplying an `earnings_case` of >= min_earnings_case_chars. Fail-open: a ticker the committed calendar does not carry is NOT MEASURED, never 'no print'.

trade_quality_requirements._min_rr_note: Raised 1.0 -> 2.0 (2026-07-16, user-approved after expectancy research): breakeven win rate at 2:1 is 33%, keeping the book profitable across the realistic 40-55% band; a 1:1 floor loses money below ~52% wins after costs (Minervini/O'Neil both demand ~2:1 at entry).
trade_quality_requirements._volatility_stop_note: A stop tighter than the name's noise is not protection - it exits on ordinary volatility, not on a broken thesis. The stop must sit at least max(min_stop_atr_multiple x 14d-ATR%, min_stop_expected_move_fraction x options expected_move%) below entry. Enforced only when volatility data is present (fail-open). If that floor exceeds max_stop_loss_distance_pct, the name is too volatile for a valid swing stop and is rejected.
trade_quality_requirements._trailing_stop_note: Chandelier exit (LeBeau/Elder; user-approved 2026-07-16): once a position's high-water mark puts (high_water - 3xATR) ABOVE the plan stop, the effective stop ratchets up with it - never down, never widened, and deliberately NO breakeven jump at +1R (research shows early breakeven moves gut trend expectancy). Forced exits fire on the effective stop; reason trailing_stop_breached when the trail was binding.
trade_quality_requirements._falsifiability_note: ADDED 2026-07-19 (audit). variant_perception, scenarios and thesis_invalidators were PRESENCE-checked only, while CLAUDE.md twice called variant_perception 'validator-enforced' - a single non-space character satisfied it. min_invalidator_chars was 12, so 'drops below 50dma' (17) passed as a binding falsifier. scenarios' probabilities need not have summed to 1, and tools/scenario_ev.py computed honest EV whose only callers were two RENDERING paths. Now: invalidating_print needs a numeric threshold, time_box needs a date or day-count, variant_perception needs a figure and a dated resolution, and scenario probabilities must sum to ~1 with a non-negative probability-weighted return. These check SHAPE, not argument quality - no regex grades a thesis, and the risk desk and the reader remain the judges of that.

theme_risk._note: Market value of positions sharing the same demand_driver plus proposed size must stay under this fraction of equity. Catches DELL+HPE style single-factor books that sector caps miss when names sit in different GICS sleeves. Fail-open if demand_driver missing (field check already rejects). The notional cap here complements the RISK-based theme cap in position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.theme_initial_risk_cap_pct.

book_risk._unknown_beta_note: ADDED 2026-08-03. The beta ceiling used to reject outright whenever ANY name in the projected book lacked a beta in the correlation feed, and on 2026-07-28 that killed a BKR BUY whose only unknown name was BKR itself against a 100%-CASH book - a $49 position on a $984 book cannot make anything a leveraged index bet, and the same trade was re-proposed and filled hours later. Failing closed on an unmeasurable input is right when the input could hide real exposure; it is wrong when the worst case is computable. Unknown betas on the PROPOSED name are now assumed to be this value (deliberately pessimistic - the ceiling itself) and the cap is enforced against that. HELD positions missing a beta still fail closed: an exposure already carried cannot be bounded by sizing, and only the one being added can.
book_risk._tradeability_note: Added 2026-07-19, both DEFAULT OFF pending evidence. Both floors currently fail OPEN on missing data: a proposal on a ticker absent from market_context skips the stop noise-band check entirely (a 1% stop on an 8%-ATR name passes), and a name with no market-cap figure clears the $1B floor by default. The enforcement is built and tested; enabling is a one-line flip once the evidence is in. require_volatility_data: a live gather covers 182/187 tickers with ZERO universe names absent, so the coverage case is already strong - held off only because 26 existing tests pass market_context={} and rewriting that many safety fixtures hours before going live is how a real assertion gets weakened by accident. Enable after a week of runs, then fix the fixtures deliberately. require_market_cap_data: weaker case and it stays off longer. market_cap_usd is NOT a bundle field (0% coverage there); orchestrator.py resolves it PER PROPOSAL from deep_fundamentals, then scan rows, then a LIVE lookup - so a yfinance hiccup would block every BUY in the run. Blocking the whole book on a network blip is a worse failure than the fail-open it replaces, and the weekly universe review already bars sub-$1B names from entering. Enable only once per-proposal resolution is observed at ~100%.
book_risk._note: Book-level risk (added 2026-07-19 after an audit found every binding constraint was arithmetic on ONE proposal while portfolio_beta / shared_left_tail / corr_to_book were computed by tools/correlation.py and consumed only as prose). Four controls, all in tools/book_risk.py, all pure. (1) max_factor_stack_pct: aggregate notional across factor_map.AI_STACK_DRIVERS. The 2% per-driver risk cap permits ~2 positions per driver, so 8 positions across 4 AI-stack drivers was 100% AI exposure passing every existing limit - a per-driver cap is not a factor cap. (2) gap_adjusted_heat: the 8% heat cap sums (cost-stop)*qty, which assumes stops FILL AT THE STOP - contradicted by execution_costs.stop_gap_atr_fraction (0.5) in this same file, and by the only closed stop in the ledger (DELL plan stop 408.00, fill 389.75, 4.5% through, realized -13.5% on a position sized for 1%). Heat now adds the modelled gap-through, using correlation only to decide how much of the book gaps on the same morning - NEVER to hand budget back, since the plain sum is already the fully-correlated case. Unknown correlation assumes the worst. (3) max_portfolio_beta: MV-weighted against EQUITY not invested capital, so a half-cash book reads as half-exposed. (4) stress_scenarios: named shocks priced against the book the proposal WOULD create; losses deliberately NOT floored at stops, because a shock worth naming is one where stops gap. driver_shocks key __ai_stack__ shocks the whole factor group. All four fail CLOSED on unverifiable inputs, matching the portfolio_heat_unverifiable precedent.

regime_gate._note: Coded regime filter (Faber 2007/2013: ~halved max drawdown over a century; user-approved 2026-07-16). When the benchmark trend is hostile (SPY below its 200DMA), new BUYs are REJECTED (regime_gate_spy_below_200dma) - exits and holds are never blocked, and existing stops keep working, consistent with the evidence that the filter's value is blocking NEW risk, not forced liquidation. Momentum-unwind detection (tools/momentum_health.py) separately halves the risk budget via position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.momentum_unwind_risk_scale rather than hard-blocking. Fail-open when regime data is absent from market_context.

learning_controls._note: Code-enforced Learning Protocol. Under min_trades_for_binding: no hard rejections from calibration_gate. At/above: high-conf inflation caps confidence; losing sector/theme buckets require calibration_exception text. Shadow book binds caution at 8 closed shadows (separate).
learning_controls._target_calibration_note: Added 2026-07-19. min_risk_reward_ratio (2.0) is the system's most rigorously justified rule - the config carries the expectancy math - and it is computed from the LLM's own target_price, which appears ZERO times in execution/exit_guard.py. Exits are stop, trail or horizon only; CLAUDE.md calls the target 'a milestone, not a tripwire'. So the gate filtered on a number nothing enforced or graded, and the model could always clear it by writing a bigger one. Targets stay NON-BINDING for exits (letting winners run is correct and literature-supported) - instead every close is graded on claimed RR vs REALIZED RR and target attainment. Binds only at min_trades_for_binding closed trades; at n=2 it reports phase 'anecdote' and withholds the binding-grade number entirely.

llm._note: Every claude -p invocation pins --model (public track record stays reproducible across CLI-default changes) and --allowedTools (exactly what CLAUDE.md instructs: Read the chart PNGs, WebSearch/WebFetch to verify catalysts). Missing block falls back to CLI defaults. Risk desk uses a kill-checklist prompt (falsifiers, theme overlap, variant perception, entry geometry).
llm._security_note: CORRECTION 2026-07-18 (audit). This block previously claimed the allowlist grants 'nothing that can write, so an injected headline can never touch the ledger'. That reasoned about the wrong threat: ledger writes were never the exposure - SECRET READS plus egress were. The bundle carries unsanitized headlines and filing prose to a model holding Read/Glob/Grep and WebFetch, and .env sat at the repo root with live broker and write-capable X tokens. Note a Read deny rule alone would NOT have closed it, because Grep prints matching lines. Fixed by moving secrets outside the working directory (tools/envload.py; Glob/Grep are cwd-scoped), plus deny rules in .claude/settings.json. Do not reintroduce a secrets file under the repo root - tests/test_secrets_hygiene.py fails the build if one appears.
llm._risk_desk_note: CHANGED 2026-07-19 (audit). The desk previously ran the SAME model as the brain on the SAME context file, so it shared the generator's priors and was anchored on its framing - a second draft, not a second opinion, while CLAUDE.md sold it as an 'independent adversarial review'. A different model is the cheapest real independence available here. The desk cannot approve anything the validator would reject; its only powers are veto and a capped haircut, so a stricter or weaker reviewer costs at most a missed trade, never an unchecked position. Revisit if veto rates look indiscriminate.

risk_controls._require_risk_desk_note: Paper track-record integrity: BUYs require adversarial risk desk when the claude CLI is available. If CLI is absent (some cloud sandboxes), BUYs are rejected (risk_desk_unavailable) rather than passing unreviewed. Set false only for emergency local dry debugging.
risk_controls._cross_node_lease_note: Advisory lease over the shared ledger, arbitrated through git so the cloud routine and a local run never trade the same portfolio.json concurrently. A scheduled run stands down if another node holds an unexpired lease; manual runs only warn (the user is deliberately driving). Fail-open on any git error - a lease must never brick the trader.

execution_costs._note: Applied to simulated fills so the paper track record is not flattered by zero trading costs. Effective slippage each way = max(slippage_bps/10000, slippage_atr_fraction x ATR%) so volatile names cost more than a flat 10bps. entry_gap_atr_fraction: an adverse open-gap on ENTRIES (buys fill higher, sells lower) approximating a next-session fill instead of the same-close the decision used. Moomoo US equities are commission-free (per-share defaults 0) but pass SEC + FINRA TAF regulatory fees on SELLS - modeled here. model_stop_gaps: a forced stop exit can fill BELOW the stop by up to stop_gap_atr_fraction x ATR to approximate overnight gap-through risk.

alpaca._note: Alpaca PAPER account adapter (execution/alpaca_broker.py). Cash-only: the 4x margin buying power is ignored; BUY notional must fit in cash. Cloud runs cannot reach the API - they queue state/order_intents.json for the execute-orders.yml Actions executor.
alpaca._price_guard_note: re-check live last trade vs entry_price_max before submitting a BUY (fail-open without a quote)
alpaca._options_note: FUTURE flag only. hard_rules still forbid options and the validator rejects non-EQUITY instruments; enabling requires an options order path in the adapter + validator rules + account options level. Kept here so the capability is visible and buildable-on.
alpaca._resting_stops_note: Added 2026-07-19. Until this, EVERY order body in the repo was type:market and stops were floats in state/portfolio.json evaluated only when a cycle ran - scripts/stop_watch.py documented the blind windows as ~2h intraday, ~17.5h overnight and ~65.5h over a weekend, and the one closed stop in the ledger filled 4.5% through its level (DELL 408.00 -> 389.75, a 1%-risk position realizing -13.5%). NOT a bracket/OTO: Alpaca rejects order_class alongside notional, and notional orders cannot be PATCHed at all, so a bracket's stop leg could never ratchet. IMPORTANT PARTIAL: Alpaca allows fractional quantities only with time_in_force=day, and notional entries leave fractional positions - so the WHOLE-SHARE portion gets a GTC stop that genuinely survives overnight, while the sub-share remainder is disclosed as uncovered rather than assumed safe.

universe.focus: AI supply chain, semiconductors, data center infrastructure, plus large-cap market leaders with an AI/tech bias

slot_depths._note: Three intraday slots are holdings+watchlist only (fast); TWO full universe deep dives, at 10:30 and 15:30 ET. Light pre-market at 6am. Evening review is news-only. Weekly market breadth is a separate Sunday --weekly-market run. 09:00/10:00 moved to 08:45/10:30 on 2026-07-25: they were the tightest pair on the board (60min) and 10:30 clears the opening range where 10:00 sat inside it. 10:30 PROMOTED to full on 2026-08-03: a holdings_watchlist run mini-scans only holdings and the published watchlist, so the ONLY moment a genuinely new name could surface was the afternoon full scan, and the book got one look per day at the whole universe at the worst possible time to act on it. 16:00 MOVED TO 15:30 on 2026-08-03, measured: the cron fires punctually (+4 min) but a full run TAKES 18-20 minutes, so a 16:00 slot COMPLETED 16:17-16:27 on every one of the days it ran - after the closing bell, every time. The old '+22 min drift' figure was never lateness; journal.log_run_summary stamps the record when a run FINISHES, so the number was the run's own duration. At 15:30 the same work decides ~15:52, before the bell. Side benefit: 14:00->15:30 stays 90 min while 15:30->17:30 becomes 120 min, the widest recovery gap on the board. FOUR files describe these slots (this one, runlib/depths.DEFAULT_SLOT_DEPTHS, runlib/analytics.expected_slots, scripts/run_cycle.sh) and they have drifted twice - tests/test_schedule_sources_agree.py now fails if you change one and forget another.

earnings_deep_dive._note: When ANY universe company reports earnings, force a FULL deep dive and promote the reporter(s) into deep-research focus. The 8:45am slot (morning) catches overnight + pre-market reporters; the 5:30pm slot (evening) catches that afternoon's after-hours reporters — 5:30 rather than 4:00 because after-hours prints are often not out by 4pm. Applies to scheduled (--auto-depth) runs; escalates that slot's depth to full only when a reporter is detected, otherwise the slot keeps its normal light/holdings_watchlist/evening_review depth.

live_prices._note: Holdings + watchlist intraday quotes are refreshed every few minutes during market hours by the live-prices Action into state/live_prices.json, and overlaid onto the bundle's daily-bar prices before stops are enforced. A snapshot older than max_age_min is NOT overlaid (a broken feed must not clobber a good daily bar) but IS flagged as stale so the run fails safe. GitHub throttles */5 crons, so real freshness is typically ~10-20 min, not 5.

weekly_market_checkin._note: Broad multi-sector scan + discovery leaders; no trading. Deep research only on holdings and a few standouts.
